# Iron deficiency

## How it showed up
Spring 2024. I'd just finished the beginner program and should have been getting fitter, but every run felt like wading through soup. Breathless on the stairs at work, which never happens. Cold hands, cracked corners of the mouth, craving ice chips from the unit ice machine (pagophagia! I literally teach this). Asked Dr. Abernathy-Kwan for bloodwork on 2024-06-04.

## The numbers
| date | ferritin (µg/L) | Hb (g/L) | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-06-07 | 9 | 112 | low, both |
| 2024-09-10 | 28 | 124 | 3 months on supplement |
| 2025-01-14 | 39 | 128 | |
| 2025-04-15 | 46 | 131 | marathon block starting |
| 2025-09-30 | 52 | 133 | peak week done |

Lab: LifeLabs on Bloor, requisition ref LL-77310. Dr. A-K's target for an endurance athlete: ferritin above 50, so I just got there.

## Why it happened
- heavy periods, diagnosed later as partly fibroids (ultrasound 2024-07-22, two small ones, nothing urgent)
- mostly vegetarian at the time, not eating much red meat at all
- running itself: foot-strike hemolysis and losses in sweat, small but real
- coffee with every meal, which blocks absorption

## Supplement
- **Ferrous bisglycinate 25 mg elemental**, alternate days, not daily. Dr. A-K showed me the study about hepcidin: daily dosing raises hepcidin and you absorb less, alternate days absorbs more in total. Also way less constipation than the ferrous sulfate 300 mg I tried first (which was awful).
- with 250 mg vitamin C or a glass of orange juice
- in the morning, empty stomach if possible, at least 2 hours away from coffee and tea, and away from calcium, so no yogurt with it
- Jamieson brand, $14.99 for 60

## Food changes
- red meat twice a week now (beef chili, lamb kofta)
- lentils and chickpeas with lemon or peppers
- cooking tomato sauces in the cast iron skillet adds a little iron, care rules in [[Cast iron care]]
- coffee moved away from meals, see [[Caffeine cutoff]]
- spinach is not the hero people think, oxalate

## Side effects
- dark stools, normal, warned Dev so he wouldn't panic
- constipation on ferrous sulfate, fixed by switching, plus psyllium ([[Fiber and gut health]])
- mild nausea if I take it right before a run, so not on long run mornings

## How it feels now
Night and day. Easy pace dropped from 7:10/km to 6:40/km at the same heart rate between June and October 2024. No more ice cravings. Still get a bit flat in the week of my period, so no hard sessions planned then if I can help it.

## Next
- ferritin recheck 2026-01, then every 6 months while training
- ask about IV iron only if it drops under 30 again. Not needed now.
- remember: donating blood is off the table until ferritin is stable above 50 for a year, Canadian Blood Services checks Hb only
